profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Highly skilled software/systems R&D monkey wrench with a 20y proven track record of successful projects and research in browsers, telecoms, transportation, aerospace and railway industries. I currently work at Google's YouTube Living Room (previously Chrome/OS Graphics, Chrome WebRTC). 

I've got an outstanding ability to identify and develop key technologies based on innovation, with a strong focus on team building and coaching to achieve goals. Finally I have an extensive experience in management consulting on identifying, designing and carrying out new products consistent with the company's overall goals and core technology.

Specialties: 
- System Engineering for Browsers and in particular Media/Real Time applications.
- Embedded and real-time software development. 
- International R&D team building and leadership, having worked in 8 countries with >15 different nationalities.
- Signal/Video/Image Processing, system engineering and research.
- Application specific ASIC/FPGA/systems V&V.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.locationName: San Bruno (CA), prev: San Jose (CA) and Mountain View (CA)
positions.description:
YouTube Living Room - TLM for the Cobalt team. We develop the Chromium fork running YouTube on Android TV, smart TVs, Apple TVs, Amazon Fire, Jio, Roku, dongles...

Previous: Google Chrome SWE on all platforms; in particular in areas related to graphics, video and real time communications. Heaps of code under mcasas@chromium.org, owner of several areas and W3C Specs. TL/M for ChromeOS Video for many years.

positions.title: Sr Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Mountain View (CA) with a few years in New York City (NY)

positions.title: Development Lead
positions.description:
I led the R&D group of Mosami: a Bell Labs supported venture to create the real time media processing engine in the cloud. My tasks included creating the vision and making it happen, while coaching the people and making sure everyone participated in the success. For Mosami and his predecessor Immersive Communications, I built the up to 10p team while creating the processes and interfacing with senior management, Bell Labs, procurement, financing, and a number of shared services. Half the team was located in the US and another half in Antwerpen.

Before that, I was leading the Sw driver design and development for in-house ASIC/FPGAs for Network Packet Processing.

positions.title: Development Lead
positions.description: Embedded software engineer and development lead for the European Space Agency (ESA): System engineering for a prototype Inertial Measurement Unit board including electronic PCB design and microcontroller-based software development, subsequently tested in real conditions in the International Space Station (ISS), see attached.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description: Engineer for the railway industry: Design and implementation of several real-time communication devices for on board and ground equipment over a range of platforms (Linux, TI DSPs, Analog Devices uCLinux).

positions.title: PhD/MSc Scholar
positions.description: Power consumption modelling and optimisation for embedded DSP, for Texas Instruments Processors belonging to the 55x and 28x families, and for Digital Signal Processing algorithm cores (FFT, IIR, etc).

volunteerExperiences.description:
I landed a bunch of patches in Gstreamer gst-plugins-bad, OpenCV concretely. Doing stuff like skin detection in video sequences, disparity etc. [1]. They should be distributed in all modern Linux distros now, see f.i.

gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! video/x-raw,width=320,height=240 ! videoconvert ! skindetect postprocess=false  ! videoconvert ! ximagesink

for a skin detection divertimento :-)

[1] http://cgit.freedesktop.org/gstreamer/gst-plugins-bad/log/?qt=author&q=Miguel+Casas-Sanchez
